name: Robert Crewe-Milnes, Marquess of Crewe
credit: No confirmed portrait sourced for this archive.
bio: Robert Crewe-Milnes, first Marquess of Crewe (1858–1945), was a British Liberal politician, statesman and writer.
The poems here are taken from Arthur Quiller-Couch's anthology The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (Clarendon Press, 1912).

poems.title: Seven Tears
poems.author: Robert Crewe-Milnes, Marquess of Crewe
poems.collection: The Oxford Book of Victorian Verse (1912)
poems.text:
To join the ages they have gone,
Those seven years, —
Receding as the months roll on;
Yet very oft my fancy hears
Your voice, — 'twas music to my ears
Those seven years.

Scant the shadow and high the sun
Those seven years;
Can hearts be one, then ours were one,
One for laughter and one for tears,
Knit together in hopes and fears,
Those seven years.

How, perchance, do they seem to you,
Those seven years,
Spirit-free in the wider blue?
When Time in Eternity disappears,
What if all you have learn'd but the more endears
Those seven years?
